newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends steady, gilt prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends steady, gilt prices firm.

text.p: Indian call money ended the first day of 1997 in the 10.75-11.0 percent range against the day's opening quotes of 10.25-11.0 percent, dealers said.
They said call rates were steady for most of Wednesday, easing slightly only towards the end of trade.

"We were expecting rates to come down earlier than they did today," said a dealer. "We are approaching the reporting day and normally rates should have eased by now. The rates are largely being driven by sentiment."
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.
Dealers said prices of government securities were firm in brisk trade.
"Security prices were up by ten paise in most securities traded today," said a dealer. He said most of the demand was for securities with maturities till 1999 and treasury bills.
Treasury bills maturing in June 1997 were traded at 10.20 percent, up from the last traded 9.80 percent, while July treasury bills yielded 10 percent, down from 10,25, he said.
